subject: Government
title: Pre-Colonial Nigerian Political Systems
outline: The Yoruba monarchical system under the Oba and Alaafin
Checks on rulers in traditional societies
Impact of colonial rule on traditional systems

modules.title: The Hausa-Fulani Emirate System
modules.html:
1. Background

The Hausa states (Kano, Katsina, Zaria, Gobir and others) were centralised monarchies long before 1804. The Sokoto Jihad of Usman dan Fodio (1804–1810) unified them into the Sokoto Caliphate, an Islamic theocratic empire with the Sultan of Sokoto as Sarkin Musulmi (Commander of the Faithful) at its head.

2. Structure

LevelOfficerFunction
CaliphateSultan of SokotoSpiritual and political head; appoints and disciplines emirs
EmirateEmirExecutive, legislative and judicial head of the emirate
AdvisoryCouncil of officialsWaziri (prime minister), Galadima (capital administration), Madawaki (army commander), Sarkin Dogari (police), Sarkin Fada (palace official), Maaji (treasurer)
JudicialAlkali courtsAdminister Sharia law; the Grand Kadi heads the system
DistrictHakimiDistrict head, collects taxes and maintains order
VillageVillage head (Dagaci)Local order and tax collection through ward heads

3. Taxation

Zakat (alms on wealth), Kharaj/Kudin Kasa (land tax), Jangali (cattle tax), Jizyah (tax on non-Muslims) and Gaisuwa (gifts/homage).

4. Checks on the Emir

The Quran and Sharia law, the advisory council, the kingmakers who selected him, the Sultan's power of removal, and the influence of the ulama (scholars). In practice the emir was powerful, which is why the British found the system convenient for Indirect Rule.

examples.q: Why was Indirect Rule most successful in Northern Nigeria?
examples.a: The emirate system already possessed everything Lugard needed: a recognised, hierarchical authority with the Emir at the apex, a functioning tax system (jangali, kudin kasa) capable of yielding revenue, an established judiciary in the Alkali courts, and a tradition of obedience reinforced by Islam. The British simply superimposed a Resident over the Emir, retained the structure and ruled through it cheaply.

examples.q: Identify the roles of the Waziri and the Madawaki.
examples.a: The Waziri was the chief adviser or prime minister who coordinated the administration and mediated between the Emir and other officials. The Madawaki was the commander of the emirate's army, responsible for defence, military campaigns and internal security.

modules.title: The Yoruba and Igbo Systems, and Comparison
modules.html:
1. The Yoruba System

The Yoruba operated a constitutional monarchy in which the Oba was sacred but checked. In the Oyo Empire:

  • Alaafin — the political head, regarded as the companion of the gods, but not absolute.
  • Oyomesi — council of seven kingmakers led by the Bashorun; they selected the Alaafin and could reject him. If they sent him an empty calabash or parrot's egg, he was obliged to commit suicide.
  • Ogboni cult — a powerful religious and judicial society that checked both the Alaafin and the Oyomesi and could veto the Oyomesi's decision.
  • Are-Ona-Kakanfo — generalissimo of the army, stationed outside the capital.
  • Ilari — palace messengers and tax officials representing the Alaafin in the provinces; Baale headed towns and villages.

2. The Igbo System

The Igbo were largely segmentary and decentralised — 'a republican society without kings' — organised around the village and village group.

  • Ofo title holders / Okpara — the eldest man of a lineage holding the ofo staff, symbol of authority and justice.
  • Village assembly (Oha-na-eze / Ama-ala) — all adult males debated matters; decisions were by consensus.
  • Age grades — performed public works, defence and enforcement of decisions.
  • Council of elders — deliberated and interpreted custom.
  • Ozo title society — conferred prestige and influence on wealthy, respected men.
  • Umuada — daughters of the lineage who settled disputes and enforced morality.
  • Oracles and priests — e.g. the Ibinukpabi (Long Juju) of Arochukwu, arbitrated grave disputes.

3. Comparison

CriterionHausa-FulaniYorubaIgbo
StructureHighly centralisedCentralised but checkedDecentralised, segmentary
HeadEmir under the SultanOba/AlaafinNo single ruler; council of elders
Religion and stateFused; Islamic theocracySacred kingship, Ogboni influenceOracles influential but no theocracy
SuccessionHereditary within ruling houses, approved by SultanRotational among ruling houses, chosen by kingmakersAchieved status by age, wealth and title
JudiciaryAlkali courts (Sharia)Oba-in-council, OgboniElders, age grades, oracles
Response to Indirect RuleVery successfulPartially successfulLargely failed — warrant chiefs resented; Aba Women's Riot 1929

examples.q: Explain why Indirect Rule failed in Igboland.
examples.a: Igbo society had no centralised chiefs to rule through. The British therefore appointed warrant chiefs — men without traditional legitimacy — and gave them powers the culture had never vested in one person: tax collection, court judgments and forced labour. Their abuses, plus the rumour of taxing women, triggered the Aba Women's Riot of 1929, after which the system was reviewed and replaced with the Native Court and later massed-benches arrangements based on village groups.

examples.q: How did the Oyomesi and Ogboni limit the Alaafin?
examples.a: The Oyomesi, seven kingmakers under the Bashorun, selected the Alaafin, advised him and could reject his policies; if he was tyrannical they sent him a symbolic empty calabash or parrot's egg, requiring him to take his own life. The Ogboni, a religious-judicial cult, checked the Oyomesi in turn: it had to confirm the rejection, preventing the kingmakers themselves from becoming tyrants. This mutual restraint approximated checks and balances.

modules.title: Features of pre-colonial political systems
modules.html:

quiz.q: The spiritual and political head of the Sokoto Caliphate was the:
quiz.solution: The Sultan, as Sarkin Musulmi, headed the caliphate and appointed emirs.

quiz.q: The Sokoto Jihad was led in 1804 by:
quiz.solution: Shehu Usman dan Fodio launched the jihad that created the caliphate.

quiz.q: The council of kingmakers in Oyo was the:
quiz.solution: The Oyomesi, seven chiefs led by the Bashorun, selected and checked the Alaafin.

quiz.q: An empty calabash sent to the Alaafin meant:
quiz.solution: It signified rejection by the Oyomesi and obliged the Alaafin to take his life.

quiz.q: The Igbo political system is best described as:
quiz.solution: Authority was dispersed among lineages, elders and age grades.

quiz.q: The ofo staff symbolised:
options: Authority and justice in a lineage
quiz.solution: The eldest man, the Okpara, held the ofo as emblem of legitimate authority.

quiz.q: The commander of the Oyo army was the:
quiz.solution: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo was generalissimo and lived outside the capital.

quiz.q: Cattle tax in the emirate system was called:
quiz.solution: Jangali was levied on herds, mainly on Fulani pastoralists.

quiz.q: Alkali courts administered:
quiz.solution: Alkali (qadi) courts applied Islamic law within the emirates.

quiz.q: The Aba Women's Riot occurred in:
quiz.solution: The 1929 riot protested warrant chiefs' abuses and fear of taxing women.

quiz.q: Warrant chiefs were introduced because Igbo society lacked:
quiz.solution: With no kings to rule through, the British created chiefs by warrant.

quiz.q: The Ogboni cult performed which key function?
options: Judicial and religious check on rulers
quiz.solution: It exercised religious and judicial authority and checked both Alaafin and Oyomesi.

quiz.q: Age grades in Igbo society were mainly responsible for:
quiz.solution: Age sets executed communal labour, security and enforcement of decisions.

quiz.q: The chief adviser or prime minister in an emirate was the:
quiz.solution: The Waziri coordinated the emirate administration.

quiz.q: Which system fused religion most completely with government?
quiz.solution: The caliphate was an Islamic theocracy in which Sharia was the law of state.

quiz.q: Umuada in Igbo society refers to:
options: Daughters of the lineage who settle disputes
quiz.solution: Umuada, the married daughters of a lineage, mediated conflicts and enforced morality.

quiz.q: The ‘Lycée’ system was part of the colonial education policy of?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: France.

quiz.q: In French colonial policy, the ‘Policy of Association’ eventually replaced?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Assimilation.

quiz.q: The 'Warrant Chiefs' system was associated with:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Indirect Rule.

quiz.q: Capitalism is an economic system characterized by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Private ownership.

quiz.q: Apartheid was a system of institutionalized racial segregation in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: South Africa.

quiz.q: A ‘Single-member constituency’ system is often called?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: First-past-the-post.

quiz.q: The ‘Apartheid’ system was a policy of racial segregation practiced in?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: South Africa.

quiz.q: The ‘Cabinet’ (where ministers are also legislators) is primarily found in which system?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Parliamentary.

quiz.q: What is ‘Checks and Balances’?
options: Each arm of government limiting the powers of the others
Checking the time of legislative sessions
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Each arm of government limiting the powers of the others.

quiz.q: ‘Theocracy’ is rule by?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Religious leaders.

quiz.q: ‘Autocracy’ is rule by?
options: A single person with absolute power
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: A single person with absolute power.

quiz.q: The current Secretary General of the UN (2023) is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Antonio Guterres.

quiz.q: Federalism involves:
options: Sharing of power between center and units
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Sharing of power between center and units.

quiz.q: The EFCC deals with:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Financial crimes.

quiz.q: A referendum is a vote on:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: A specific public issue.

quiz.q: The AU replaced the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: OAU.

quiz.q: The head of the Judiciary is the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: CJN.

quiz.q: The 1979 Constitution established the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Presidential system.

quiz.q: Delegated legislation refers to laws made by...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Administrative bodies and executive agencies.

quiz.q: The 'Collective Responsibility' of the cabinet is a feature of...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Parliamentary system.

quiz.q: A bicameral legislature is one that consists of...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Two houses.

quiz.q: The right to vote in an election is known as...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Franchise.

quiz.q: The 1929 Aba Women's Riot was primarily caused by...
options: Introduction of taxes on women and the Warrant Chief system
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Introduction of taxes on women and the Warrant Chief system.

quiz.q: The 1946 Richards Constitution was criticized because...
options: It was forced on Nigerians without consultation
It gave too much power to the Sultan
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: It was forced on Nigerians without consultation.

quiz.q: Non-alignment as a foreign policy meant...
options: Neutrality during the Cold War between USA and USSR
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Neutrality during the Cold War between USA and USSR.

quiz.q: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was replaced by the African Union (AU) in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: 2002.

quiz.q: The ECOWAS treaty was signed in 1975 in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Lagos.

quiz.q: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: New York.

quiz.q: Independence of the Judiciary is ensured by...
options: Judges being appointed by the military
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Security of tenure for judges.

quiz.q: The 'Unification Decree' 34 of 1966 was promulgated by...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Aguiyi Ironsi.

quiz.q: Diplomacy is the...
options: Conduct of international relations through negotiation
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Conduct of international relations through negotiation.

quiz.q: Which of these is a function of the Legislature?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Law making.

quiz.q: The 1922 Clifford Constitution introduced:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Elective Principle.

quiz.q: The non-aligned movement was formed to:
options: Remain neutral during the Cold War
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Remain neutral during the Cold War.
